name: Gemini 3.1 Flash Live Preview

output: text (a transcript of the audio; the response modality must be audio)

voice.input_audio: Raw 16-bit PCM, little-endian, mono, 16 kHz native, resampled if the MIME type states the rate; images and video as JPEG frames, at most 1 frame a second [gemini-live-capabilities, gemini-live-overview]
voice.voices: Prebuilt voices shared with Google's text-to-speech models; no count given for the Live API [gemini-live-capabilities]
languages: The model page lists no languages. The capabilities guide lists 99 languages for the Live API in general [gemini-spec-3-1-flash-live, gemini-live-capabilities]
voice.turn_detection: Server-side voice activity detection is on by default (realtimeInputConfig.automaticActivityDetection). Settings: start_of_speech_sensitivity, end_of_speech_sensitivity, prefix_padding_ms and silence_duration_ms. The server default for silence is about 800 ms, and Google advises 500 to 800 ms [gemini-live-capabilities]. Automatic detection can be turned off (disabled: true). The client then sends activityStart and activityEnd, and Google advises a client silence threshold of at least 500 ms. A hybrid mode keeps server detection for the start of speech and lets a client detector send audio_stream_end for a fast end of turn [gemini-live-capabilities]. The client sends audioStreamEnd when the microphone pauses for more than one second [gemini-live-capabilities].
voice.interruption: Barge-in is supported. When detection hears the user during output, the server cancels the generation, discards pending function calls and sends interrupted: true. The client must drop its queued playback audio at once [gemini-live-capabilities, gemini-live-best-practices].
voice.latency: Time to first audio on Artificial Analysis's Big Bench Audio set: 0.96 seconds at minimal thinking and 2.99 seconds at high [aa-speech-to-speech]. A forum report of 2026-09-05 describes 9 to 15 seconds on the Live API serving path for this model, down from about 1 second [forum-31-latency]. Google publishes no figure.
voice.session_limit: Without context window compression an audio-only session ends after 15 minutes and an audio-plus-video session after 2 minutes. With compression and session resumption a session can run without a time limit. One connection lasts about 10 minutes, and the server sends GoAway before it closes the connection. Resumption handles stay valid for 2 hours after the session ends. The session context window is 128k tokens [gemini-live-capabilities, gemini-live-session]. On Gemini Enterprise Agent Platform the limit is 1,000 concurrent sessions per project on pay-as-you-go, and GoAway comes 60 seconds before the end [gemini-cloud-live-session].

pricing_usd_per_mtok.notes: Gemini API pricing page, paid plan, standard rate. Input: text $0.75, audio $3.00 (about $0.005 a minute), image or video $1.00 (about $0.002 a minute). Output: text $4.50, audio $12.00 (about $0.018 a minute), and the output price includes thinking tokens. The input and output fields of this card hold the audio rates. Audio counts 25 tokens a second [gemini-live-best-practices]. Each turn bills the whole session context again, so the cost of a turn grows with session length [gemini-live-best-practices]. Turning on audio transcription adds text output tokens at the text rate. Search grounding: 5,000 free requests a month shared across Gemini 3.x models, then $14 per 1,000 requests. The free plan costs nothing and Google may use its data to improve products; the paid plan is not used for that. One table covers gemini-3.8-live, gemini-3.8-live-extended-thinking and gemini-3.1-flash-live-preview [gemini-pricing]. No caching, no batch.
